title: MessagesStore sent row is still the unsanitized caller map
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (MessagesStore::post_inbox_from, get_sent, get_sent_id)

nqes allowlisted the inbox document. The sent HashMap still does sent.insert(assigned_id, Value::Map(map)) on the decoded caller map after from-rebind, canned expansion, and id assign.

GET /msg/sent and GET /msg/sent/{id} therefore echo untrusted extra keys and untyped optional fields. Spec 18.1.1 types: to tstr, ack bool, priority uint 0..2, reply_to uint, ttl uint, ts uint. post_inbox_from only type-checks body/text (tstr), canned (known uint), and id (uint unique). ack=1, priority=99, ttl=-1 (as a CBOR integer stored verbatim), to as a nested map, and arbitrary extra keys are stored and returned.

This is a first-vs-schema split vs spec 18.1.1 and vs the inbox path that now persist only {id, from, ts, body}. Python MessagesResource also keeps the caller dict for sent; spec is the arbiter.

Fix: persist an allowlisted sent record (spec 18.1.1 keys only). Type-check optional fields and reject (4.00) mismatches, including priority outside 0..2. Drop unknown keys.

Perspectives: security, correctness.
